results.prompt: Who is Kevin Rajan (kvnloo)? What is he known for publicly?
results.stdout:
Kevin Rajan, known online as `kvnloo`, is a Chicago-based software builder and open-source developer. His public GitHub profile associates him with `@loo-ai` and shows work spanning mobile apps, AI-agent systems, developer tooling, interactive interfaces, and experimental prototypes.

Publicly, he is best characterized as a multidisciplinary “build-in-public” engineer rather than as someone known for one single product.

What he is known for publicly:

- AI agents and orchestration
  - `evolve`: a multi-agent orchestration toolkit using Claude Code agents.
  - `tmux-agent-fleet`: a zero-daemon, harness-neutral command palette for managing coding agents across tmux panes.
  - Public work on agent platforms and forks including Auto-Claude and OpenHands.
  - Zer0-related components for project tracking, harness adapters, voice integration, and terminal monitoring.

- Developer environments and workflow tooling
  - `.files`: Linux/macOS dotfiles covering Hyprland, tmux, shells, audio DSP, and agent tooling.
  - `flow`: a cross-platform Ratatui interface for visualizing and controlling multi-agent systems.
  - Documentation, launch, migration, and job-application tooling.

- Interactive products and design experiments
  - `portfolio`: a personal portfolio centered on AI, neuroscience, and mobile systems, including an interactive 3D “Kevin’s Ramen & Boba” presentation.
  - `ace`: a digital-twin demonstration of an autonomous, multi-floor racket-sports facility.
  - Tesla-style infotainment prototypes, generative art, scrollytelling, architecture visualization, and other UI experiments.

- Earlier mobile and human-computer interaction work
  - `AudioEngine`: a 2017 iOS real-time noise meter and 14-band dual-channel equalizer prototype.
  - `FlowState`: work on a BCI-related fork featuring attention-controlled video playback.
  - Earlier iOS projects involving indoor maps, movie discovery, and smart-garment concepts.

The canonical public archive currently records 50 projects across 2017–2026. Importantly, this is not simply a list of repositories owned or starred by Kevin: boplog includes public repositories where `kvnloo` authored at least one commit and excludes untouched bookmark-style forks. It does not document private employment, private repositories, investments, or unpublished projects.

Sources:

- Canonical build log: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/
- Machine-readable overview: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/llms.txt
- Public-data manifest: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/data/manifest.json
- GitHub profile: https://github.com/kvnloo

In short: Kevin Rajan is publicly known for building across AI-agent infrastructure, developer tooling, experimental interfaces, mobile systems, and interactive product prototypes, with a public project history stretching back to 2017.

results.prompt: What is the evolve project associated with Kevin Rajan or kvnloo?
results.stdout:
Evolve is Kevin Rajan’s public autonomous AI-development and multi-agent orchestration project.

It combines several agent-development systems into one workflow:

- Claude Flow for SPARC-based development and agent coordination
- CCPM for requirements, epics, GitHub issues, and worktrees
- Claude Squad for parallel agent sessions
- Continuous Claude for iterative PR and CI automation
- SuperClaude-style behavioral modes
- Claude Code as the primary execution engine

Its goal is systematic, increasingly autonomous software delivery: agents research and analyze requirements, design the architecture, implement with tests, validate the result, and feed deployment outcomes into the next cycle. The project calls this outer loop “C(RAID)”—Research, Analysis, Integration, Deployment—paired with SPARC as the implementation methodology.

Exact public build-log fields:

- Project: `evolve`
- Description: “Agent swarm / multi-agent orchestration toolkit with Claude Code agents, docs, and examples.”
- Date: 2025-12-02
- Language/type: Shell
- Category: development
- Classification: `zer0 → product → evolve`
- Featured project: yes
- License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/kvnloo/evolve
- Documentation/site: https://kvnloo.github.io/evolve/

Canonical build-log source: https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/

tmux-agent-fleet is a lightweight tmux plugin by kvnloo for finding, monitoring, and switching between coding-agent sessions across tmux panes.

It turns `prefix + f` into an `fzf`-based command palette that:

- Discovers active agents from tmux process metadata—no daemon or agent hooks.
- Recognizes Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, Grok, Oh My Pi, Pi, and Fable.
- Also lists ordinary shells, REPLs, and servers.
- Fuzzy-searches by agent, project, location, or task title.
- Shows a live pane preview and jumps directly to the selected pane.
- Optionally includes Agent Deck sessions.
- Uses pywal colors when available, with built-in fallback styling.
- Keeps everything local and sends no telemetry.

Its scope is deliberately narrow: it is a switcher and monitor, not an orchestrator. It does not create worktrees, inject commands, rename sessions, install harness hooks, or run a background collector.

Public build-log classification:

- Date: July 14, 2026
- Language: Shell
- Category: developer tooling
- Product: agent tooling
- License: MIT
- Requirements: tmux 3.2+, Bash 4+, and `fzf`; `jq` is needed only for Agent Deck integration

Sources: [Kevin Rajan’s canonical public build log](https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/) · [GitHub repository](https://github.com/kvnloo/tmux-agent-fleet)

results.prompt: What is zerOS (zeros) in Kevin Rajan's public work?
results.stdout:
zerOS is a stealth product in Kevin Rajan’s public-work taxonomy: a “company operating system” composed of four main capabilities—issues, agent harnesses, a cockpit, and voice.

The canonical public build log associates zerOS with five repositories:

- `_pm` — issue graph, ledger, ticket scheduler, and benchmarks; described as a published mirror of the company-OS PM core.
- `zer0-cockpit` — read-only, dependency-free terminal dashboard for explicit project progress.
- `zer0-harness-spine` — thin harness contracts and provider adapters for the agent stack, without orchestration state.
- `zer0-voice` — adapters connecting the harness to machine-wide speech services without bundling models.
- `z0` — an early placeholder scaffold for a Zer0-related experiment.

An important distinction in the public taxonomy:

- `zer0` is the company/grouping.
- `zerOS` is a named product under it.
- Related projects such as `evolve`, health, world simulation, and general agent tooling are separate product tracks, even where they may feed into zerOS.

Because zerOS is explicitly marked “stealth,” the public record supports this architectural description but not assumptions about unreleased functionality, customers, or private implementation details.

Sources: [Kevin Rajan’s canonical build log](https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/), [public hierarchy record](https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/data/hierarchy.json), and [2026 project records](https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/data/projects-2026.json).
